what: CME Group runs futures and options exchanges. It owns the markets where interest-rate, equity-index, energy, metals and agricultural futures trade, and it clears those trades itself, standing between buyer and seller.
customers: Banks, hedge funds, asset managers, commodity producers and active traders worldwide.
money: a fee on each contract traded and cleared
moat: Liquidity concentrates in one venue: traders go where other traders already are, and open positions can only be closed on the same exchange, which makes moving nearly impossible.
risks: Volumes fall when markets are calm, and the company does not control volatility
Competitors have tried to launch rival futures venues with lower fees
Regulatory changes to clearing or margin rules affect the model
Growth is slow in a mature market
opportunities: Operating margins above 60% mean extra volume drops almost straight to profit
Interest-rate uncertainty keeps hedging demand high
It pays a regular dividend plus a variable annual dividend from surplus cash
watch: Average daily volume by product group, particularly interest-rate futures.
